**UK banks launch shared digital identity service for app-based KYC**

*Major UK banks are building a joint digital identity tool to streamline remote customer verification, though questions about liability, commercial model and overlap with open banking data remain unresolved.*

A consortium of UK banks has announced a shared digital identity service designed to let customers verify their identity remotely through banking apps. The group includes several of the same institutions that collaborated on open banking infrastructure and the now-retired Paym mobile payment registry, suggesting the initiative draws on established interbank cooperation channels.

The service aims to reduce friction in know-your-customer processes by allowing banks and potentially third parties to rely on identity credentials already held by a customer's bank. If it reaches scale, it could reshape how onboarding works across financial services and beyond, particularly for sectors such as gambling, telecoms and government services that face increasing pressure to improve identity verification.

Several practical questions remain conspicuously open. Who carries liability when a shared credential is used by a third party and proves wrong? How will the service be funded, given that open banking already provides much of the underlying account data for free? And who will drive adoption beyond the founding banks? The UK government's recent proposal to use open banking for social media age verification hints at the policy appetite for bank-verified identity, but a workable commercial model has yet to emerge.

*Sources: [UK banks unite on new digital ID tool for apps](https://www.fintechfutures.com/biometrics-id-verification/uk-banks-unite-on-new-digital-id-tool-for-apps) — FinTech Futures | [UK bank ID scheme seeks to transform remote KYC, but who pays, and what happens when...](https://www.retailbankerinternational.com/comment/uk-bank-id-scheme-transform-remote-kyc/) — Retail Banker International*
